examples.ko: 냉장고를 사려고 무이자 할부 행사를 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm waiting for an interest-free installment event to buy a refrigerator.

examples.ko: 이 카드는 석 달 무이자로 결제할 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this card you can pay interest-free over three months.
It's interest-free, so I decided to buy it without worry.

examples.ko: 이 상품은 무이자가 아니라서 수수료가 있어요.
examples.en: This item isn't interest-free, so there is a fee.
I thought it was interest-free, but a fee was added.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 무이자 육 개월 할부가 돼요.
examples.en: That store offers six-month interest-free installments.

explain: 쇼핑에서는 거의 '무이자 할부'로 나와요. 반대는 '유이자'보다 '이자가 붙다'처럼 풀어서 말하는 경우가 더 많아요. 광고에는 '수수료'가 따로 붙는 경우도 있으니 조건을 꼭 확인하세요.

phrases.example: 이자 없이 석 달 동안 나눠서 낼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can pay in installments for three months with no interest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무이자'를 풀어서 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain way to say 무이자.

phrases.en: Interest-free loans have strict conditions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 빌릴 때 이자가 없는 경우에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for loans that carry no interest.

phrases.en: I'll pay with the 3-month interest-free plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카드 결제에서 개월 수와 함께 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to say it at checkout, with the number of months.

explain_en: In shopping it almost always appears as '무이자 할부' (interest-free installments). For the opposite, people more often say '이자가 붙다' than a single word. Ads may still add a separate fee, so check the conditions.

examples.ko: 영화를 만들려면 먼저 물주를 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: To make a movie, you first have to find a backer.

examples.ko: 그 사업의 물주가 누구인지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows who is bankrolling that business.
My older brother is paying today, so order whatever you like.

examples.ko: 물주가 갑자기 손을 떼서 공사가 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The financier suddenly pulled out, so construction stopped.

examples.ko: 좋은 물주를 만나서 가게를 열 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I met a good backer and was able to open a shop.

examples.ko: 친구가 물주 노릇을 하면서 밥을 샀어요.
examples.en: My friend played the role of the one paying and bought us a meal.

explain: '투자자'보다 가볍고 입말에 가까운 말이에요. 친구 사이에서는 오늘 돈을 내는 사람을 농담으로 '물주'라고도 해요. '물주를 찾다', '물주 노릇'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 새 가게를 열려고 물주를 구하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm looking for a backer to open a new shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물주를 찾다'와 비슷한데 필요한 사람을 얻으려 한다는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 물주를 찾다, with more of a sense of securing the person you need.

phrases.en: I'll play the big spender today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구 사이에서 돈을 내는 역할을 농담처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking way to say someone is the one paying among friends.

phrases.en: Today's moneybags is Minsu, who just got paid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그날 돈을 내는 사람을 가볍게 부르는 입말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken phrase for whoever is paying that day.

explain_en: It is lighter and more colloquial than '투자자' (investor). Among friends, the person paying today is jokingly called the '물주'. It appears in forms like '물주를 찾다' and '물주 노릇'.

t90.ax: Nobody knows who is bankrolling that business.

en: to be stingy; to be inhospitable; to be ungenerous

examples.ko: 그 식당은 인심이 박해서 반찬이 적어요.
examples.en: That restaurant is stingy, so there are few side dishes.
The teacher graded harshly, so I am upset.

examples.ko: 사장님이 월급에 너무 박한 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the boss is too stingy with salaries.
That critic is harsh when rating movies.

examples.ko: 박하게 굴지 말고 후하게 좀 주세요.
examples.en: Don't be stingy, give a little more generously.

examples.ko: 이웃에게 박하지 않은 분이라 모두 좋아해요.
examples.en: He is not stingy with his neighbors, so everyone likes him.

explain: 인심, 점수, 평가, 대우처럼 남에게 주는 것이 적고 야박할 때 써요. 반대말은 '후하다'이고, '박하'(민트)는 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: The judges gave a stingy evaluation, which was disappointing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박한'이 평가나 점수 앞에 오면 좋게 봐 주지 않고 야박하다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before words like evaluation or score, 박한 means ungenerous and unwilling to be lenient.

phrases.en: That boss treats his employees ungenerously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 대하는 태도가 정이 없고 인색할 때 써요. '박하게'가 '대하다' 같은 동사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone treats others coldly and ungenerously, with 박하게 modifying a verb like 대하다.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 인심이 박하지 않아서 늘 덤을 줘요.
phrases.en: This shop isn't stingy, so they always give extras.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 야박하지 않고 넉넉하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative form it means not stingy, in other words fairly generous.

explain_en: It is used when what is given to others, such as kindness, grades, ratings or treatment, is small and cold. The opposite is '후하다', and '박하' (mint) is a completely different word.

t90.ax: That critic is harsh when rating movies.

en: to send back (mail or a parcel to the sender)

examples.en: The address was wrong, so they sent the package back.
Please send this mail back to the sender.

examples.ko: 받는 사람이 없으면 우체국에서 물건을 반송해요.
examples.en: If there is no recipient, the post office sends the item back.

examples.ko: 잘못 온 상품은 어떻게 반송하면 돼요?
examples.en: How do I send back an item that came by mistake?

examples.ko: 이사 간 사람에게 온 편지를 우체국에서 반송했어요.
examples.en: The post office sent back a letter addressed to someone who had moved away.

examples.ko: 서버 오류 때문에 반송 메일이 하루에 수십 통씩 들어와요.
examples.en: Because of a server error, dozens of bounced emails come in every day.

explain: '돌려보내다'와 같은 뜻인데, 우편물·택배·메일처럼 이미 보낸 것이 돌아오거나 돌려보낼 때 써요. 산 물건을 가게에 돌려줄 때는 '반품하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I sent the wrongly delivered letter back to the post office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말이고, 우편물뿐 아니라 사람이나 다른 물건에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word, usable for people and other things, not only mail.

phrases.en: The parcel was returned because the address was wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반송하다'의 피동 표현으로, 보낸 우편물이나 택배가 되돌려지는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of 반송하다, describing a sent item being returned.

phrases.en: This email was handled as returned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우편이나 메일을 돌려보내는 절차를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the procedure of returning mail or email.

explain_en: It means 'to send back', used for mail, parcels and emails that are sent back or returned to the sender. When you give a purchased item back to a shop, '반품하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The company paid compensation to the victim.
I was due to receive compensation because of the accident.
How much the damages will be hasn't been decided yet.
The court ruled that a large sum in damages be paid.
I took out a loan to raise the money for the damages.

examples.ko: 보험으로 배상금 일부를 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can pay part of the damages with insurance.

explain: '배상금'은 잘못으로 남에게 끼친 손해를 돈으로 갚을 때 쓰고, 비슷한 '보상금'은 적법한 일로 생긴 손해나 수고를 돈으로 줄 때 써요. 도로 공사로 땅을 내놓고 받는 돈은 '보상금'이에요.

phrases.en: The victim demanded compensation from the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손해를 입은 쪽이 돈을 달라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the injured party asks for money.

phrases.en: I broke a window and had to pay compensation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못한 쪽이 돈을 내야 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person at fault has to pay.

phrases.en: I was surprised because the compensation amount was so large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배상금이 얼마인지 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for talking about how much the compensation is.

explain_en: '배상금' is money paid for harm caused by a fault, while the similar '보상금' is money given for a loss from a lawful act. Money you get for giving up land for a road is '보상금'.

t90.ax: The company paid compensation to the victim.

en: to compensate; to pay for damage

examples.ko: 사고를 낸 사람이 피해를 배상해야 해요.
examples.en: The person who caused the accident has to pay for the damage.
The company compensated the customer for the loss.
I'll pay for the window I broke.
The court ruled that the hospital must compensate the patient.

examples.ko: 배달 중 망가진 물건은 업체가 배상해요.
examples.en: The company pays for items damaged during delivery.
If you make up for the damage, I'll forgive you.

explain: 남의 잘못으로 생긴 피해를 돈으로 갚을 때 쓰고, 사고·계약·소송에서 자주 나와요. '보상하다'는 적법한 일로 생긴 손실을 갚을 때, '배상하다'는 잘못으로 생긴 손해를 갚을 때 써요. 일상에서 물건 값을 물을 때는 '물어주다'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I demanded compensation for damages.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 계약 문제에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in accidents and contract issues.

phrases.en: The company paid the compensation money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배상으로 내는 돈을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for money paid as compensation.

phrases.en: I paid for the plate I broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 잘못으로 생긴 값을 낼 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday word for paying for something you damaged.

explain_en: It is used when paying money for harm caused by someone's fault, and often appears in accidents, contracts and lawsuits. 보상하다 is for making up a loss caused by a lawful act, while 배상하다 is for damage caused by a wrongful act. In daily life, 물어주다 (to pay for what you broke) is also very common.

dis.h: pay for damage you caused; legal tone
gh: make up for loss; broad, not only legal

p.n: 보상 is looser and does not stress legal liability for causing the damage.

t90.ax: I'll pay for the window I broke.

en: to repay; to pay off; to liquidate

examples.ko: 남은 빚을 다음 달까지 변제해야 해요.
examples.en: I have to pay off the remaining debt by next month.

examples.ko: 일부만 변제해서는 계약을 끝낼 수 없다고 변호사가 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The lawyer told me I can't end the contract by repaying only part of it.

examples.ko: 그는 오 년에 걸쳐 빚을 모두 변제했어요.
examples.en: He paid off all his debt over five years.
I talked with the bank about how to repay the money.
What do I do if I don't have the money to repay?

examples.ko: 빚을 다 변제하면 신용 등급도 올라가요.
examples.en: Once you pay off all your debt, your credit rating goes up too.

explain: '갚다'와 같은 일이지만 법, 계약, 은행 이야기에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '빚을 갚다'라고 하고, '채무 변제', '변제 기한'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I paid back the money I borrowed from my friend today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변제하다'와 같은 일을 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말로 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday word for the same thing as 변제하다.

phrases.en: I repay the loan in monthly installments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 은행 빚을 갚을 때 쓰고, '변제하다'보다 대출에 더 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for paying off bank debt; more common with loans than 변제하다.

phrases.en: The repayment deadline is next Friday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계약서나 법률 이야기에서 갚아야 하는 날짜를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in contracts or legal talk for the date by which a debt must be repaid.

explain_en: It describes the same act as '갚다' but in a stiff tone used for law, contracts and banking. In daily life people say '빚을 갚다', and the noun appears in phrases like '채무 변제' and '변제 기한'.

t90.ax: He paid off all his debt over five years.

examples.en: He paid bail and was released.
The bail was so expensive that it was hard to raise.
The court set bail at fifty million won.
They sold the house and used the money for bail.

examples.ko: 보석금은 재판이 끝나면 돌려받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get the bail money back after the trial ends.
His family set about raising the bail money.

explain: 반짝이는 '보석(jewel)'과는 관계없는 말이에요. 재판을 받는 사람이 풀려나기 위해 법원에 내는 돈이라서 뉴스나 드라마에서 들어요. 집을 빌릴 때 내는 '보증금'과는 달라요.

phrases.en: The family struggled to come up with the bail money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 돈을 구해 놓는다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting together the money needed.

phrases.en: He was released on bail before the trial.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보석'은 보석금을 내고 풀려나는 일을 뜻하기도 해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 보석 here means release on bail; common in the news.

phrases.en: The trial ended, so I got the bail money back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건을 지키면 낸 돈을 돌려받는다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting the money back after meeting the conditions.

explain_en: It has nothing to do with '보석' meaning jewel. It is money a defendant pays to the court to be released, so you hear it in news and dramas. It is different from '보증금', the deposit you pay when renting a home.

examples.en: A service charge is added separately on the bill.
This restaurant does not charge a service fee.
This price includes a 10 percent service charge.
Do I have to pay the service charge separately at a hotel?
With the service charge added, it comes to more than I expected.
I checked the bill to see how much the service charge was.

explain: 호텔이나 고급 식당 계산서에 따로 적혀 있는 서비스 요금이에요. '서비스 요금'이라고도 해요. 한국은 팁 문화가 거의 없어서, 이 돈이 팁 대신이라고 생각하면 돼요.

phrases.en: This is a price that includes the service charge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계산서나 메뉴판에서 가격 안내를 볼 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in price notes on bills and menus.

phrases.en: At a hotel, you have to pay the service charge separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 지불한다는 뜻의 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic expression for paying the charge.

phrases.en: A 10 percent service charge is added.
phrases.nuance_ko: '봉사료'와 같은 뜻으로 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word with the same meaning as 봉사료.

explain_en: It is the service fee written as a separate line on bills at hotels and upscale restaurants. People also say '서비스 요금'. Tipping is not a common custom in Korea, so you can think of this as taking the place of a tip.

examples.en: The company covers the transportation cost.
I'll cover the meal bill.
Who paid for the repairs?
If we split it in half, the load gets lighter.
The person who will bear the cost has been decided.
Everyone has to share the tax burden together.

explain: '부담하다'는 비용이나 책임을 자기가 맡을 때 써요. 돈을 낼 때는 '내다'보다 공식적이에요. '비용을 부담하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The company covers the training costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.

phrases.en: The company pays my tuition for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 위해 대신 내 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when paying for someone else.

phrases.en: We split the meal cost in half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나누어 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sharing the cost.

explain_en: 부담하다 is used when you take on a cost or responsibility yourself. It is more formal than 내다 (to pay). It appears in phrases like '비용을 부담하다' (to bear the cost).

examples.en: A construction company is selling new apartments.
The owner gave away the puppies for free.
I went to the model house to see the apartments for sale.

examples.ko: 고양이를 분양하려고 키울 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I want to give my cat away, so I'm looking for someone to take it in.

examples.ko: 올해 분양한 집은 벌써 다 팔렸어요.
examples.en: The homes put on sale this year have already sold out.
They aren't puppies raised for giving away.

explain: 새 아파트를 처음 파는 건 '분양하다'이고, 이미 산 집을 다시 파는 건 '팔다'예요. 반려동물을 다른 집에 보내 줄 때도 '분양하다'라고 하는데, 이때는 돈을 받을 수도 있고 무료일 수도 있어요.

phrases.en: I bought a new apartment from the developer last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분양하다'는 파는 쪽이고, '분양받다'는 사는 쪽이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 분양하다 is from the seller's side; 분양받다 is from the buyer's side.
phrases.en_equiv: to buy a new home (or a pet) from the seller

phrases.en: Someone is giving away cats for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반려동물을 돈 없이 다른 집에 보낼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when sending a pet to a new home for free.

phrases.en: This apartment is on sale now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 집을 지금 팔고 있다는 말로 광고에서 많이 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says new homes are being sold now; common in ads.

explain_en: A developer selling new apartments for the first time is '분양하다'; reselling a home you own is '팔다'. It's also used for finding homes for pets, either free or for a fee.

examples.en: I pay my insurance premium on the 25th of every month.

examples.ko: 적금을 십 년 동안 꾸준히 불입했어요.
examples.en: I steadily paid into my savings plan for ten years.
If you pay the membership fee all at once, they give a discount.
I went to the bank to pay money into my pension.

examples.ko: 불입할 금액을 미리 통장에 넣어 두세요.
examples.en: Put the amount you have to pay into your account in advance.

examples.ko: 아직 첫 달 보험료도 불입하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I haven't even paid the first month's premium yet.

explain: 보험료, 적금, 연금처럼 정해진 날에 나눠서 돈을 넣을 때 써요. 은행이나 보험 이야기에 나오는 말이라 친구와 말할 때는 '내다', '넣다'를 많이 써요. '납부하다'는 세금이나 요금에도 쓰는 더 넓은 말이에요.

phrases.en: The installment is automatically withdrawn from the account every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 날에 넣는 돈을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the money paid in on the set date.

phrases.en: Office workers pay into their pension every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보험료 말고 연금에도 쓸 수 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing usable with pensions, not just insurance premiums.

phrases.en: I put money into my savings plan every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구와 말할 때 '불입하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say it with friends instead of '불입하다'.

explain_en: It is used for putting money in on set dates, such as insurance premiums, savings plans and pensions. It belongs to bank and insurance talk, so with friends people say '내다' or '넣다'. '납부하다' is broader and also covers taxes and bills.

t90.ax: I went to the bank to pay money into my pension.

examples.ko: 잃어버린 강아지를 찾아 주신 분께 사례금을 드렸어요.
examples.en: I gave a reward to the person who found my lost puppy.

examples.ko: 분실물을 찾아 주면 사례금은 얼마쯤 드리는 게 좋을까요?
examples.en: How much should I give as a reward for returning a lost item?

examples.ko: 주인이 사례금으로 오만 원을 주려고 했어요.
examples.en: The owner tried to give me fifty thousand won as a reward.

examples.ko: 사례금이 걸려 있어서 많은 사람이 찾아 나섰어요.
examples.en: Because a reward was offered, many people went out to search.

examples.ko: 그분은 사례금을 받지 않겠다고 해서 선물을 드렸어요.
examples.en: They said they wouldn't accept a reward, so I gave them a gift.
They held out an envelope, saying it was a thank-you payment.

explain: 고마움을 표시하려고 주는 돈이에요. '수고비', '사례비'와 비슷하게 쓰지만 분실물을 찾아 주거나 도움을 받았을 때 특히 자주 말해요. 받는 사람이 거절할 때는 '마음만 받을게요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The owner offered a reward for the lost bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾아 주는 사람에게 주겠다고 미리 약속할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when promising a reward in advance to whoever finds something.

phrases.en: I returned the wallet, but I didn't accept a reward.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도와준 사람의 입장에서 돈을 받는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Speaks from the helper's side about receiving money.

phrases.en: I gave a small payment to the person who helped me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사례금'과 비슷하게 쓰지만 일을 도와준 데 대한 고마움의 돈이라는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '사례금', but feels like thanks for help with some task.

explain_en: It is money given to show thanks. It is close to '수고비' and '사례비', but is especially common when someone returns a lost item or helps you. A person who declines might say '마음만 받을게요' (I'll just accept the thought).

en: personal expense; one's own money (out of pocket)

examples.ko: 선생님이 사비로 학생들에게 책을 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher bought books for the students with her own money.
I paid for the business trip out of my own pocket.
I spent my own money to hold the event.

examples.ko: 사비로 산 물건은 회사에서 돌려받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get back from the company what you bought with your own money.
He had a hard time because he used so much of his own money.

examples.ko: 감독님이 사비로 선수들에게 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: The coach treated the players to meals out of his own pocket.

explain: 회사나 단체의 돈이 아니라 내 돈으로 낸다는 뜻이에요. 반대로 회사 돈은 '공금', 회사가 내 주는 비용은 '경비'라고 해요. '사비를 털다'처럼 아낌없이 쓴다는 표현도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I spent my own money for my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아끼지 않고 내 돈을 많이 쓴다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds like spending a lot of your own money without holding back.

phrases.en: I prepared the event at my own expense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사 돈이 아니라 내 돈으로 일을 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means doing something with your own money instead of the company's.

phrases.example: 사비로 간식을 사서 팀원들에게 나눠 줬어요.
phrases.en: I bought snacks with my own money and shared them with the team.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사비로' 뒤에 사다, 내다 같은 동사가 자주 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 사비로 is often followed by verbs like 사다 or 내다.
phrases.en_equiv: to buy with one's own money

explain_en: It means paying with your own money rather than a company's or group's. The opposite is 공금 (company funds), and costs the company covers are 경비. You'll also hear 사비를 털다 for spending freely out of pocket.

examples.ko: 상속세 때문에 집을 팔았다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that someone sold their house because of inheritance tax.

examples.ko: 상속세는 물려받는 재산이 많을수록 더 많이 내요.
examples.en: The more property you inherit, the more inheritance tax you pay.

examples.ko: 부모님 재산을 받으면 상속세를 내야 해요.
examples.en: If you receive your parents' assets, you have to pay inheritance tax.
Don't miss the deadline for filing the inheritance tax.

examples.ko: 그 부자는 상속세만 수십억 원을 냈어요.
examples.en: That rich person paid billions of won in inheritance tax alone.
The government announced a plan to reduce the inheritance tax.

explain: 세상을 떠난 사람의 재산을 물려받을 때 내는 세금이에요. 살아 있는 사람이 미리 주는 경우에는 '증여세'라고 해서 둘이 짝으로 자주 나와요. 주로 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 들어요.

phrases.en: I inherited a house and paid inheritance tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재산을 물려받은 사람이 세금을 낼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for when the person who inherits property pays the tax.

phrases.en: Inheritance tax rates differ by country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 계산하는 비율을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the rate at which the tax is calculated.

phrases.example: 상속세 신고는 정해진 날까지 해야 해요.
phrases.en: You have to file your inheritance tax by the set date.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 나라에 알리는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the act of reporting the tax to the government.

explain_en: It is the tax paid when receiving the property of someone who has died. When a living person gives property in advance, it is called '증여세', and the two often appear as a pair. You mostly hear it in news and economic talk.
